Is it even legal to refuse legal tender?

Not ... really. Businesses are free to refuse to take cash, but they have to explicitly inform you of that fact before the transaction begins. If they do not do this, and you offer cash in exchange for goods or services, and they say "no", they are breaking the law.
So, unless they follow the script, it would come down to "free stuff or I call the cops?" Neat!

Again, not ... really.

For one thing, local law enforcement does not have jurisdiction to enforce Federal laws. This is a good thing. For example, if local law enforcement did have this power, they could drop an Endangered Mud Slug™ on your property (like they would a baggie of crack on a person they just shot), declare the spot where they dropped it to be a Wetland™, and then say "you are in violation of the Endangered Species Act and the Federal Protected Wetlands Act, so we are going to seize your property and sell it".

For another thing, you are offering to exchange legal tender for goods and services, not receive them for free. Either both halves of the transaction complete, or neither of them do; and in the latter case the proper remedy would be a lawsuit, not an arrest, because a violation of the Legal Tender Act is not a crime. It is unlawful, but it is a civil violation--what in legalese is called a "tort"--, not a crime.
